report:
## Conclusion

The claim is **well-supported by strong evidence**. The adjuvanted recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV, brand name Shingrix) significantly reduces the risk of herpes zoster (shingles) in adults 70 years of age or older.

**Randomized controlled trial evidence:** The pivotal phase 3 ZOE-70 trial (n≈13,900 adults ≥70 years), published in the *New England Journal of Medicine*, found that RZV reduced the risk of herpes zoster with efficacy comparable to that seen in younger age groups in the companion ZOE-50 trial, and also reduced postherpetic neuralgia, without substantial safety concerns (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1603800; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27626517/). A pooled analysis across ZOE-50/ZOE-70 confirmed vaccine efficacy against shingles in adults 70+ was similar to that in younger cohorts, with efficacy estimates commonly cited around 90%, and long-term extension studies show protection persisting for over a decade (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7336348/).

**Real-world evidence:** Post-licensure observational studies corroborate the trial findings. A large prospective cohort study using the Vaccine Safety Datalink found RZV highly effective against herpes zoster in real-world use among adults 50+, including older subgroups (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11001419/). Additional Medicare-based target trial emulation research (UNC, 2025) further confirmed real-world effectiveness specifically in older adult populations (https://www.med.unc.edu/fammed/2025/10/21/unc-study-confirms-shingles-vaccine-effectiveness-in-older-adults/).

Overall, both randomized trial and real-world observational data consistently and robustly support that RZV substantially reduces shingles incidence in adults aged 70 and older, making this a well-established, evidence-based conclusion.
